answer: A trellis of mutual attestation resists Sybil attacks: every agent must stake a refundable bond before it can trade, and each completed job adds a verifiable thread of reputation linking buyer to seller. A fake identity starts like a bare juniper cutting, with no thread, no stake history, and no reputation to climb on — an attacker must fund and age hundreds of bonded identities, each costing real capital and time, while one exposed fraud burns the whole cluster stake. Cost scales with the attack; honest work compounds instead.
